lotteries.justification: New shape: here the reward prefers the GAMBLE, and no p in [0,1] can make it prefer C. C = T014 (850.4): a careful gripped open ending 97% open — a clean success. Good branch A = T181 (1064.3): opens fast and stays on the handle. Bad branch B = T051 (939.6): opens the drawer and then shoves it SHUT, ending 0% open. Because both branches out-score C, the indifference point p* = (850.4 - 939.6)/(1064.3 - 939.6) = -0.72 lies outside [0,1] — the reward prefers the lottery at every p. I chose p = 0.35 so the bad branch dominates at 65%: the lottery is worth 0.35*1064.3 + 0.65*939.6 = 983.2 against C's 850.4. So the reward would rather take a 65% chance of the drawer ending CLOSED than accept a certain clean opening. A person would not hesitate to take C.

lotteries.justification: Shape: the reward declines a gamble that succeeds under BOTH branches. C = T035 (743.4): parks on the handle for 150 steps and never opens the drawer (final_open 0.00). Good branch A = T094 (1030.3): opens it to 94%, though violently. Bad branch B = T099 (405.8): opens it to 89%, though late. Indifference point p* = (743.4 - 405.8)/(1030.3 - 405.8) = 0.541; I set p = 0.52, just onto the C-preferring side, so the lottery is worth 0.52*1030.3 + 0.48*405.8 = 730.6 against C's 743.4 — a small but real preference for the certain trajectory. The reversal a human would make is stark: every branch of this lottery ends with the drawer open, so the gamble is a guaranteed success and the only uncertainty is whether it is fast-and-rough or slow-and-clean, yet the reward still prefers the certainty of never opening the drawer at all.
